stimulus.source_note: Benjamin Franklin, “Join or Die,” Pennsylvania Gazette, May 9, 1754, public domain.
stimulus.text: A 1754 cartoon by Benjamin Franklin shows a snake cut into eight pieces, each labeled with the initials of a colony or group of colonies — S.C., N.C., V., M., P., N.J., N.Y., and N.E. — beneath the words “JOIN, or DIE.”

figures.alt: Benjamin Franklin's 1754 'Join or Die' cartoon — a snake cut into eight labeled pieces beneath the words JOIN, or DIE
figures.caption: Benjamin Franklin, “Join or Die,” 1754

source: original; stimulus image from the shared pool, Benjamin Franklin, “Join or Die” (1754), public domain
stem: Franklin published this cartoon in the spring of 1754, on the eve of the Albany Congress. Which of the following best explains why the Albany Plan of Union failed?

options.text: The British government in London vetoed the plan because it gave the colonies too much power over trade.
options.misconception: London did reject the plan, but the plan died first in the colonial assemblies, which refused to give up their right to tax themselves.

options.text: The French and their Native American allies threatened to attack any colony that joined the union.
options.misconception: The French were the threat the plan was meant to meet, not opponents of the plan.

options.text: No colonial legislature would give up its power to tax itself or accept rule by a single intercolonial government.
The colonies had already agreed to unite under the Articles of Confederation, so the plan was unnecessary.
options.misconception: The Articles of Confederation came in 1777, more than twenty years after the Albany Plan failed.

rationales.A: London did reject the plan, but the plan died first in the colonial assemblies, which refused to give up their right to tax themselves.
rationales.B: The French were the threat the plan was meant to meet, not opponents of the plan.
rationales.C: Franklin's plan would have created one intercolonial government with the power to tax for defense, but every colonial legislature that considered it said no. Background: the colonies guarded their right to tax themselves jealously, and none would hand that power to a new body it did not control. The cartoon's warning came true in reverse: the colonies stayed divided, and the plan died where it was born — in the assemblies themselves.
rationales.D: The Articles of Confederation came in 1777, more than twenty years after the Albany Plan failed.
rationales.general:
1. Look at the snake. Eight pieces, eight separate colonies — the cartoon's whole point is that the colonies are divided.
2. Ask what the plan needed. One government that could tax all the colonies for their common defense.
3. Ask what the colonies would not give up. The right to tax themselves — the power every assembly guarded most jealously.
4. Put it together. A union that took away self-taxation was dead on arrival in every legislature that saw it.
Remember: in 1754 the colonies would not unite even to defend themselves — unity had to be learned the hard way.
